dek: Submissions are failing, scores are crawling and the bell rings Monday night. CPMP calls it a circus, Tufa’s Jeroen Cottaar is timing the missing forty minutes with a stopwatch, and the NVIDIA seven are stuck in the same traffic as everybody else.
discord: SATURDAY SPECIAL: Kaggle’s circus weekend. CPMP called the ARC contests a circus, Tufa’s Jeroen Cottaar is timing Kaggle’s missing forty minutes, Giba and the NVIDIA seven are stuck in the same traffic, and V | A | M gained 26 points in five days. https://arc.markbarney.net/news/2026-10-31-evening-arc-2-preview
headline: Saturday Special: Kaggle’s circus weekend, CPMP’s roar and the detective of Tufa

sections.heading: Welcome to the circus
sections.text: Two days to the bell and Kaggle’s biggest show has gone sideways. In ARC-AGI-3, competitors report submissions dying with system errors or finishing in half an hour with a flat zero. In ARC-AGI-2, scores take more than a day to come back, so last-day submissions may never count. The answer from the hosts and Kaggle staff: the deadline stands. Ours too: Monday, 11:59 pm UTC. Nobody has said it louder than Jean-François Puget, CPMP, who quoted our no-extension bulletin Saturday morning with one word for the weekend: circus. The full showdown, with Kaggle’s answer: https://arc.markbarney.net/news#2026-10-31-saturday-nvbanana-grandmasters

sections.heading: The detective of Tufa
sections.text: Friday night we met Jeroen Cottaar in the Tufa Citadel. Saturday he is running experiments. His team’s empty-notebook tests say every submission loses forty to fifty minutes before the notebook even starts, and that the time counts against the nine-hour budget. CPMP says a delay before a notebook runs is not uncommon. Two of the sharpest minds in the field, politely at odds: https://arc.markbarney.net/news#2026-10-31-saturday-cottaar-forty-minutes

sections.heading: The NVIDIA seven
sections.text: In ARC-AGI-3 the separate seven-person NVARC3 team sits eighth: CPMP, Darragh Hanley, Ivan Sorokin, Elad Sarafian, Gal Kaplun, Yeyin Zhu and Giba, who once ranked No. 1 on all of Kaggle. Meet the squad and see CPMP pointing toward Chen’s rabbits and Tufa’s banner in our juggernaut illustration: https://arc.markbarney.net/news#2026-10-31-saturday-nvarc3-juggernaut. The two competitions have different rosters and standings.

sections.heading: Meanwhile, in the top ten
sections.text: Chan Kha Vu’s V | A | M gained 26 points in five days and is ninth on the ARC-2 board at 76.25, with a loud voice in the scoring fight. Points, not places: https://arc.markbarney.net/news#2026-10-31-saturday-chan-vam-top-ten
